description: Reproducible CCEL source for Matthew Henry's "Commentary on the Whole Bible" (originally published 1706-1721, public domain). Published by CCEL as 6 separate volume files (unlike JFB's single file, and unlike Calvin's 45 single-book files) -- each volume covers several consecutive Bible books. No raw XML is committed to git (data/raw/ is gitignored); fetch with scripts/build_commentary_database.py --henry-fetch, which downloads each volume's url and verifies raw_sha256 before use. Each entry in 'books' names one div1 (one canonical Bible book) within its own volume file; div1 ids are only unique within a single volume (e.g. 'Ez' means Ezra in volume 2 but Ezekiel in volume 4), so lookups must be volume-scoped. Matthew Henry personally wrote Genesis through Acts (44 books: all of volumes I-V, plus Acts in volume VI). Romans through Revelation (22 books) was completed posthumously after Henry's 1714 death by named continuing ministers, per volume VI's own preface and its table of contributors -- each such book's contributor_raw_name is that real author's name as the source states it, and authorship_note quotes the source's own account. This is real, source-stated per-book attribution, not inferred.

volumes.title: Commentary on the Whole Bible Volume I (Genesis to Deuteronomy)
Commentary on the Whole Bible Volume II (Joshua to Esther)
Commentary on the Whole Bible Volume III (Job to Song of Solomon)
Commentary on the Whole Bible Volume IV (Isaiah to Malachi)
Commentary on the Whole Bible Volume V (Matthew to John)
Commentary on the Whole Bible Volume VI (Acts to Revelation)

known_empty_commentary_divs.reason: Upstream CCEL markup artifact, confirmed identical in all 5 one-chapter books of the Bible (Obadiah, Philemon, 2 John, 3 John, Jude) and in no other book: the chapter's own opening <scripCom> carries passage text "Ob 1" (a bare book+chapter label, meant as a chapter-only heading marker like every other book's) but is mis-coded with a verse-1-specific osisRef instead of a chapter-only one, and is immediately followed by a completely empty <div class="Commentary"> (zero children -- no quoted text, no prose). The real, complete commentary on this verse immediately follows as the next proper range (which does carry the quoted-passage paragraph and prose). No content or passage coverage is lost by treating this specific empty div as a documented, audited no-op rather than a parse failure.

books.title: Romans
books.authorship_note: Matthew Henry died in 1714 having completed his own exposition through the Gospels and Acts (Acts is filed under CCEL's Volume VI split for pagination only -- per Volume V's own preface footnote it was originally part of Henry's own Matthew-Acts manuscript). Per Volume VI's preface ("Preface: Acts to Revelation") and its own table of contributors, the exposition of Romans was completed after Henry's death by Mr. John Evans, not by Matthew Henry -- named explicitly in that table, not inferred. Traditionally published and cited as part of "Matthew Henry's Commentary," but this book's own words are Mr. John Evans's.
